newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban retreat from parts of northern city.
newsitem.headline: Taleban retreat from parts of northern city.

text.p: Afghan Taleban fighters were forced out of many areas of the newly conquered northern Afghan city of Mazar-i-Sharif on Wednesday in fierce fighting with their opponents, witnesses said.
They said some fighters of the purist Islamic militia had been disarmed but some units remained in the city.
A lull settled over the city after more than 15 hours of fierce fighting in wide areas of the city, but sporadic shooting and explosions could still be heard at noon.
A witness said at least 20 bodies of Taleban fighters lay in the streets and many vehicles had been wrecked in the clashes.
The violence broke out on Tuesday when a Taleban column of tanks and armoured personnel carriers moved into the mainly Shi'ite Moslem northern district of Saidabad.

The fighting erupted just after a meeting between Taleban leaders including Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous and ethnic Uzbek General Abdul Malik, whose troops were supposed to be operating jointly with the Taleban.
